# Stickfps

A 5v5 round-based browser tactical FPS: Counter-Strike round/economy structure, Krunker-style
movement feel, procedurally-generated low-poly stickmen. Server-authoritative hit registration,
ephemeral 6-character room codes, AI bots, two cosmetic maps, anonymous auth only, zero PII, zero
persistence beyond a match.

Alongside [[farely]] this is one of only two non-coursework products in the source set — and the only
one with a real-time networked server.

## Architecture

Two processes that share no code. Client sends **intent only** — `PlayerInput` carries movement
axes, jump, crouch, yaw and a client tick and **no position**; `FireRequest` carries weapon id,
origin, direction and tick and **never a hit result**. `Room.resolveFireRequest` is documented
in-code as "the only method in this codebase that decides which player a shot hit (C1)".
See [[server-authoritative-netcode]].

- 60 Hz [[fixed-timestep-simulation]] on both sides — server uses a drift-corrected recursive
  `setTimeout`, explicitly not `setInterval`; client uses a `useFrame` accumulator capped at 5
  steps per frame.
- [[client-side-prediction-and-reconciliation]] by blend-toward-snapshot; full input-replay is
  explicitly out of scope for v1.
- [[entity-interpolation]] renders remote players 100 ms in the past from a 2-snapshot buffer.
- Sim code is **deliberately duplicated** rather than extracted into a shared workspace package —
  see [[duplicate-sim-code-over-shared-package]].
- All match state is in-memory per `Room`. Nothing persists. {{supabase}} does exactly one thing:
  anonymous sign-in.
- Every visual and audio asset is generated in code — [[no-external-assets]].

## Verified, and what is thinner

Verified: 108 server + 52 client vitest tests, 2 Playwright specs, `tsc` and `oxlint` clean,
`vite build` clean, a real Docker build/run/`/healthz` cycle, a real WebSocket smoke test, and
genuine Playwright captures of a live bot match at 1600×900. Server tests cover the authority
surface densely — fire gating, friendly fire, buy validation, hit zones, grenade physics, perk
tiers, round transitions, zombie-player cleanup, room-code format.

Thinner, and stated as such in the repo itself ([[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]):
the checked-in E2E covers **only the lobby**; the two-browser combat playtests of rounds 8–9 ran
from scratchpad scripts and were never committed; no live pentest; no forged-packet fuzzing; no
10-player profiling ("no profiling tooling was available in the environment this was built in");
hosted Supabase never tested. `confidence: medium` on the test counts — they rest on
`PROGRESS.md`'s own reporting, with no CI and no coverage artefact.

## Dead ends and things that broke

`PROGRESS.md` is the highest-value document in the repo for exactly this reason — see
[[progress-md-as-build-log]] for the full round-by-round list. The sharpest:

- **Round 5: no `reload-request` existed on the wire at all.** Client reload was purely cosmetic, so
  every weapon was permanently empty server-side after its first magazine; later shots were silently
  rejected while the HUD showed full ammo.
- **Round 3: `WeaponRig` had never rendered a gun mesh** — it `return null`ed for two rounds.
- **Round 5: nothing tracked round wins**, so the match winner was literally undeterminable.
- **Five authority loopholes** found in one round: dead players could still fire, firing was accepted
  in lobby and buy phase, the server did not track the equipped weapon (so a modified client could
  alternate weapons to beat both cooldowns), `joinRoom` never left the previous room (immortal
  zombie players holding 60 Hz loops alive), and movement had no bounds at all.
- **Client-origin raycast vulnerability**: the server passed the client-reported shot origin straight
  into the raycast — "muzzle-to-forehead against a player across the map".
- **±π yaw seam** made remote players spin a full 360°; **lighting broke twice**.
- **Whole transport replaced** in round 11 — [[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]].
- **Grayscale film-noir art identity retired** after being a mandatory hard constraint in three
  documents — [[superseded-in-place-documentation]].

Reported and deliberately not fixed: kill-feed entries can drop when two lethal hits land in one
React batch; ~1.4 MB bundle; both teams spawn stacked; no per-connection rate limiting; environment
props have no collision and do not block bullets (a named scope cut, SRS FR-9.4); round win is
elimination-only; bots use neither grenades nor perks.

## How it was built

[[spec-driven-development]] end to end: an IEEE-830-adapted SRS with FR/NFR ids and a traceability
matrix, then a `docs/specs/task-<id>.md` per phase, then code, then independent verification. The
loop itself is committed — [[architect-coder-tester-loop]] and
[[agent-skills-checked-into-the-repo]] (91 files of vendored Three.js skill packs and authored
subagent definitions).

Also an instance of [[readme-as-guided-tour]], [[generated-audit-artifact]] and — the repo's most
systematic flaw — [[documentation-drift]].
